items.note:
Confirmed: the talk was on 9 Sep 2019, 11:15–12:00. arXiv v1 is 2020-02-29T17:42:48Z with the MPHYS10 comment. The proceedings PDF was created 2020-04-22 (Last-Modified 2020-05-18).

Refuted: four claims, namely 'no slides were found', 'only the 2019 talk title is documented', the summary's 'documented, by title only', and 'the earliest written statement still dates from 29 February 2020'. The slides are public at http://mphys10.ipb.ac.rs/slides/Minic.pdf. They are linked as '(abstract, slides)' on the lecturers page that the finder itself saved (scratch/s-conf/data/sites/mphys10_p_lecturers.html).

They are 25 handwritten pages with no text layer. I decoded the JPEG 2000 images and read them visually, so they cannot be checked by code:
- PDF p. 24: 'Each particle of the Standard Model has a "dual" particle … Dual particles → dual Standard Model (hidden sector?)'; 'Metaparticles Φ(x,x̃) → dark matter quanta correlated to visible (baryonic/Standard Model) quanta'.
- PDF p. 25: 'Dark matter Φ(x, x̃), [x, x̃] ≃ iλ²'. In ∫√(−g g̃)[L_m(x) + L_m(x̃)], the term L_m(x̃) ≃ L̃_m(x) is marked 'dark matter sensitive to Λ and L_m(x)'.

Dating of the slides:
- PDF CreationDate 2019-08-29.
- Server Last-Modified 10 Sep 2019 14:52:47 GMT.
- First Wayback capture 2019-09-19 06:42:42 UTC. It is truncated at 1 MiB but byte-identical to the first 1,048,576 bytes of today's file, and its recorded original length (3,125,429) and Last-Modified match.

So the identification was public in writing 163–172 days before the arXiv posting (computed). The finder's 'about 5½ months' from talk to posting is 173 days, 5.68 months (computed).

Three earlier venues of the talk named in the acknowledgement can be dated, all under the title 'Manifest quantum non-locality …':
- PTRel 5: 26 Sep 2018.
- Bangkok: 9 Jan 2019.
- IGC@25: 27 June 2019.
The 2018 slides have no dual Standard Model, so MPHYS10 remains the earliest documented statement found.

overall:
I checked all 25 items against sources I fetched myself. Every quotation the finder gives was found again by code in text I extracted. Four quotations in arXiv v1 of Minic 2020 match only when spacing is ignored, because pypdf splits words there. All dates were confirmed against Indico pages, the arXiv API, INSPIRE, server headers or PDF metadata.

**Main refutation (item 2, and the overall's 'one nuance').** The finder says three things: no slides of Minić's MPHYS10 talk were found, the 2019 talk is documented 'by title only', and 'the earliest written statement still dates from 29 February 2020'. All three are wrong.
- The slides are public at http://mphys10.ipb.ac.rs/slides/Minic.pdf. They are linked '(abstract, slides)' on the lecturers page the finder itself saved.
- They state the identification as a proposal:
  - 'Each particle of the Standard Model has a "dual" particle … Dual particles → dual Standard Model (hidden sector?)'.
  - 'Metaparticles Φ(x,x̃) → dark matter quanta correlated to visible (baryonic/Standard Model) quanta'.
  - L_m(x̃) is marked 'dark matter sensitive to Λ and L_m(x)'.
- The server dates the file 10 Sep 2019. The first Wayback capture, 19 Sep 2019, is byte-identical. So the identification was public in writing 163–172 days before the arXiv posting (computed).
- The slides are handwritten images. I read them visually after decoding; they cannot be checked by code.
- Three venues named in the paper's acknowledgement came earlier, all under the title 'Manifest quantum non-locality …': PTRel 5 (26 Sep 2018), Bangkok (9 Jan 2019) and IGC@25 (27 Jun 2019). The 2018 slides present metaparticles as 'non-particle dark matter with Milgrom's scaling', with no dual Standard Model. So MPHYS10 remains the earliest documented statement found.

**Label corrections.** Two 'evidence-against' labels are stronger than their evidence:
- Graesser 2023, for the C4 shared-photon form.
- Fischer, Brümmer et al. 2026, for C1's monopole form.

Each weighs only against a version #11 already sets aside: unhidden position-localized analogs in the first case, #14's ordinary-kinematics model in the second (flag 68). Graesser's setup, and Chitose–Ibe's, also bear on the separate-photon form (related).

**Smaller corrections.**
- The Balaji title is 'An Exciting Dark Matter Solution …', not 'Excited'.
- Winn's SUSY 2025 talk was 19 Aug 2025, 17:50 US/Pacific. The finder's 20 Aug is the UTC date.
- Several of the finder's 'talks' are posters: Ho–Takahashi at COSMO19 and SI2019, both PLANCK2026 entries, and Deng–Boyle at PASCOS 2026.
- INSPIRE merges Popławski's MG16 paper with an arXiv preprint whose own comment calls it a Springer book chapter.
- Two items recorded as title-only have slides: Minić at Pheno 2012 and Ng at DSU 2018. I read both. Neither identifies a dual sector, so the finder's conclusions stand.

**One overall statement needs a qualifier.** 'The only conference statements of dark matter as the dual counterpart of visible matter come from the school' is too broad. Winn 2025 ('a Dual to ordinary matter', one magnetically charged partner per Standard Model particle, as dark matter) is such a statement under electric–magnetic duality, and the mirror-matter talks are under parity. The school's statements are the only ones in the phase-space/T-duality sense.

**Confirmed.**
- The 'correlated' clause and 'neither form'. My brief extra search found nothing on the velocity-gated χ, p-localized monopoles, or C2, C3, C6 or C7.
- The refusals: Fermilab Indico and meetings.aps.org return Cloudflare 'Just a moment…' (HTTP 403), and agenda.infn.it runs an Anubis bot check. None was bypassed.
- Four of the finder's hit counts reproduce exactly.

**One C5-related item was missed** in CERN Indico: cosmologically coupled black holes as a dark-energy component (IberiCos 2025).
